g.text: FP4 with block scales: the E2M1 ladder, MXFP4, NVFP4, and DeepSeek's KV variant
E2M1: eight magnitudes (plus sign). Spacing 0.5, then 1, then 2.
A block whose max is 3.1 with a power-of-two scale (E8M0): scale rounds
up to 1, the max lands at 3.1 -> 3, and rungs 4 and 6 are never used.
With an E4M3 scale of 3.1/6 the max lands on 6 and the whole ladder is used.
MXFP4 block (OCP): 32 elements, one power-of-two scale
NVFP4 block: 16 elements, one E4M3 scale, plus one FP32 scale per tensor
9 bytes = 4.5 bits per element (+ 4 bytes per tensor)
DeepSeek-V4.1 main KV entry: 512 channels = 32 NVFP4 blocks, no tensor-level scale
512 x E2M1 = 256 bytes of nibbles (32 blocks of 16 channels)
total 288 bytes per entry (FlashMLA 'V4.1 fp4' row), against 1,152 in bf16 and 528 in FP8
Why no tensor scale: the latent is RMS-normalized, so |channel| <= sqrt(512) ~ 22.6 (observed ~10), while E4M3 x E2M1 already reaches 448 x 6 = 2688.
